newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude rebounds with WTI, diffs idle.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude rebounds with WTI, diffs idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rebounded late Thursday and ended just above Wednesday values, while local differentials idled.
Spot prices for December West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 10 cents over Wednesday in reaction to a NYMEX heating oil rally.
Dec heating oil finished the day a steep 2.20 cents higher at 73.40 cents a gallon.
With basis WTI higher and discounts flat at $2.20 a barrel, Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude edged up 10 cents to $22.00/22.30 a barrel.
A higher NYMEX price for crude helped turned away ANS buyers, who saw the grade's discount shrink to $2.20 a barrel earlier this week from $2.30 last month.
A trader for a Pacific Northwest refinery said the company was considering further run cuts after trimming production by 5,000 barrel-per-day last month.
Weak margins are keeping refiners out of the market, traders and analysts said.

West Coast players said they dismissed Wednesday's API report which showed a five-million-barrel-decrease in the region's supplies. Much of the decrease involves waterborne supplies which are difficult to track, according to traders.
Line 63 crude remained thinly traded in typical early month discussion.

Wilmington crude was $17.60/$17.70 a barrel, while bids for Kern River crude rose 10 cents to posting levels after traders said they saw higher prices for deals. Kern was talked $16.25/$16.35 a barrel.
